title: fix(plugin-audit,plugin-approvals)!: refuse a query over activity text, ledger snapshots or the approval snapshot for a reader withheld a field of its record (#21154)
body:
Fixes #21154
Clause-②: no (narrowing)

A filter, search, sort, grouping or aggregation over a column that carries another record's field values is now refused, in the engine's own refusal shape, for a non-system reader whose security answer withholds any field of that record's object, and for any non-system reader when the query names no single parent object. Before this, the read-time redactions narrowed only what a row SERVES, so the predicate selected on the stored value at rest: row presence answered a probe one guess at a time, and a group key handed the stored text back. Triage ruling `5929903631` (option A), applied to every member the measurement reached (claim `5930307463`, amended `5931964383`).

## The family, by member

| Member | Columns (by class) | Measured before | Folded here |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| Activity stream | the text, the record label, the recorded change | predicate answers by row presence; grouping returns the stored value | yes (the card) |
| Approval request, generic data door | the submitted-record snapshot | predicate answers by row presence; grouping returns the stored snapshot | yes (H4) |
| Compliance ledger | the before and after snapshots | predicate answers by row presence; grouping returns the stored value | yes (amendment, seat 2's note `5931903481`) |

## Per-class table — generic data door, real boot

Readers of #21081's three field classes (a field served masked, a capability-gated field with no mask, a field the reader's sets do not grant), one reader per class, plus the unrestricted reader as the control. Every restricted class read the same in every row, so the classes share a row; each class has its own pins. Status and code only.

| Reader | Column class | Probe | Before | After |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| each restricted class | activity text / label / change | matching filter, parent named | 200, rows | 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED` |
| each restricted class | activity text / label / change | non-matching filter, parent named | 200, no rows | 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED` |
| each restricted class | activity text / label / change | filter naming no parent | 200, rows or none | 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED` |
| each restricted class | activity text / label / change | grouping (query door) | 200, stored value as the group key | 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED` (aggregate words) |
| each restricted class | activity text / label / change | sort | 200 | 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED` |
| each restricted class | activity (searched set) | free-text search, matching or not | 200, rows or none | 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED` |
| each restricted class | ledger before / after | matching and non-matching filter, parent named or not | 200, rows or none | 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED` |
| each restricted class | ledger before / after | grouping; sort; search | 200 (grouping returns the stored value) | 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED` |
| each restricted class | approval snapshot | matching and non-matching filter, parent named or not | 200, rows or none | 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED` |
| each restricted class | approval snapshot | grouping | 200, stored snapshot as the group key | 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED` (aggregate words) |
| restricted reader, on a parent it is served in full | activity label, ledger snapshot | matching and non-matching filter | 200, rows or none | 200, rows or none (unchanged) |
| control (unrestricted) | every column above, parent named | matching and non-matching filter, grouping, sort, search | 200, rows or none | 200, rows or none (unchanged) |
| control (unrestricted) | every column above, no parent named | filter, search | 200 | 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED` (the pin rule, see H2) |
| any reader | a query naming no value-bearing column | list | 200 | 200 (unchanged) |
| any restricted class | activity columns | analytics door, grouping dimension | 200, stored value | 200, stored value — not closed here, see Acceptance notes |

H5, the refusal matched: the engine's own answer for a non-queryable field of the parent object, measured on the same boot, is 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED` with its predicate words (a filter or sort) or its aggregate words (a grouping). The new refusals carry the same code, status (`status` and `statusCode`) and first sentence, naming the guarded column, followed by one sentence naming the remedy. They name nothing about the parent's fields.

## H2 — which parent, and why

Rule: the query must pin ONE parent object, by equality on the parent-object column at the root of its filter (or inside a root `$and`), and the reader must be served every field of it. A query that pins none is refused for every non-system reader whenever the security service is wired.

Why not "any parent the query can reach" as the code stands: the only per-query knowledge of parents is the activity read gate's pre-scan, which runs the caller's own filter. Its parents are those of the rows a query MATCHES, so a matching probe would reach the withholding parent and be refused while a non-matching probe reached none and answered an empty list: the refusal itself would be the oracle, and the ruling's "matching and non-matching both refused" pin fails. A probe-independent reach needs a new scan of every parent the table names, which is a third mechanism; it is raised as an open question in the report instead. The pinned rule is the fail-closed one, and widening it later is not a breaking change. It is the shape the approvals service door already took for its free-text arm (#11040): no authority, unchanged; authority wired, one known object or nothing.

"Served every field" is read from the serve seams themselves, never derived a second way: the activity redaction's served set (also used for the ledger) and the approval redaction's served set, asked as the caller, compared with the security service's read projection as the system. A serve seam's "no answer" (no security service) passes, since the rows are then served whole.

## Mechanism

- `plugin-audit`: `parent-field-query-guard.ts`, one engine read middleware per object (activity stream, compliance ledger), registered with ONE call in `AuditPlugin`, ahead of the activity read gate so a refused query pays no pre-scan. `activity-field-redaction.ts`, `audit-writers.ts` and `index.ts` are not changed.
- `plugin-approvals`: `payload-predicate-guard.ts`, registered beside the snapshot redaction middleware.
- Clauses judged: the engine predicate guard's set — `where` and `having` (keys and cross-field comparands), `orderBy`, `groupBy`, `aggregations` (field and filter). A free-text search arrives expanded into `where`. The projection is not judged.
- Operations: `find`, `findOne`, `count`, `aggregate`. System-context and context-less reads are not judged.

## Pins (synthetic fixtures; no title states a value or a column)

- `plugin-audit` `activity-predicate-guard.test.ts` (40) and `audit-log-predicate-guard.test.ts` (27): real kernel, engine, driver and plugin, security double; per class a matching and a non-matching probe refused, count, grouping, sort and search refused, the control and the served-in-full parent unchanged, no-security unchanged, fail-closed, and the guard's column list held equal to the redaction's own strip.
- `plugin-approvals` `payload-predicate-guard.test.ts` (19): real engine and driver, guard mounted by the plugin's own `start`.
- dogfood `activity-text-predicate.dogfood.test.ts` (21): real boot with the real security plugin, one reader per class plus the control, all three members, armed before measuring.

## Local gates at `dcb051ea7c`

One locked script: the 68 families `dispatch-gates --commands` derives from this diff, reconciled with `--ran` (68 derived, 68 run, exit codes recorded, 0 not measured), plus every touched package's tests and typecheck and the dogfood suite.

- 67 of 68 families exit 0; `check:system-context-census` exits 1 (see Acceptance notes).
- `plugin-audit` 478 / 478 and typecheck 0; `plugin-approvals` 823 / 823 and typecheck 0; dogfood typecheck 0; dogfood pins 38 / 38; dogfood suite 1302 passed, 3 skipped.

## Acceptance notes

- **`check:system-context-census` is red, by design of this claim's surface.** Both new middlewares read the system flag, so the census page needs two anchors (the two guards' registration functions, in the plugin-audit row and the approvals row of the page's lane 1 and lane 4 tables) and its counts regenerated (`gen:system-context-census --fix`). That page is outside this claim's file surface, and PR #21171 edits it too, so it is left for the seat.
- **Analytics door, not closed here.** The ad-hoc analytics query over the activity stream still groups by a value-bearing column and returns the stored value, before and after: its native-SQL strategy runs no engine read middleware. #21080 (in flight) routes objects that carry a read middleware off that path; the guard is then reached by construction (the engine `aggregate` refusal is pinned here). Not measured after #21080.
- **The no-parent rule is broad by choice.** Measured: an unrestricted reader's free-text search over the compliance ledger or the activity stream that names no parent object, previously answered, is now refused, because both objects' searched sets include their value-bearing columns. The alternative (judge every parent the table names) is raised in the report.
- **Shared files with PR #21171 (open).** `audit-plugin.ts` (one registration here) and the import of the served-set composition from `activity-field-redaction.ts`, which #21171 moves to a new module: whichever lands second merges `main`, re-points that import and re-runs its pins.
- Filter-array spelling: a single-condition array reaches the guard (refused); a compound array spelling is refused earlier as malformed.
- A pin by membership (`$in`) or by more than one object is not accepted; that would be a widening.
- The clause walk is restated in the two plugins because neither depends on the security plugin's predicate guard. Carrier: none.
- The no-middleware-seam warning in `AuditPlugin` is unchanged (one-registration constraint); without the seam the guard is not installed, like the read gate and the redaction.
- The approvals service door's own free-text rule (#11040) is unchanged.
- The branch is 8 commits behind `main`; the incoming commits touch only dependency versions in the two plugins' manifests and root dev dependencies, and the derived gate list is identical after a fetch.
